description: The Advanced AI settings page in the qontinui-runner desktop application, accessed via the 'Advanced AI' tab in the Settings sidebar. It configures four agentic subsystems: Memory Compression (token-budget management for AI context windows, preventing overflow by summarizing old knowledge entries), Retry with Feedback (exponential backoff with jitter and error-context injection into retry prompts), Intelligent Task Routing (cost/latency optimization by routing tasks to different Claude models based on file count thresholds), and Post-Run Reflection (automated post-workflow analysis that applies fixes such as knowledge base updates and workflow step rewrites). The first three subsystems are persisted together via the save_agentic_settings Tauri IPC command and loaded via get_agentic_settings. Post-Run Reflection is saved immediately on toggle via PUT /reflection/settings on the runner's HTTP API — it has no separate Save button. All four sections are collapsible and start expanded by default. A 'Reset to Defaults' button restores the first three subsystems in-memory without saving; 'Save Agentic Settings' commits them to disk.

groups.name: Page Structure
groups.description: The Advanced AI tab renders a page header with Brain icon, a descriptive subtitle, four collapsible section panels, and two action buttons at the bottom. This group verifies the top-level structure after settings load.

assertions.description: The heading 'Advanced AI Features' is displayed at the top of the Advanced AI tab
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded (loading indicator is gone)

assertions.description: The description text beginning with 'Configure intelligent agentic features including memory compression, automatic retry with feedback injection, and task-based model routing' is visible below the heading
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: All four section headers are present on the page after load: 'Memory Compression', 'Retry with Feedback', 'Intelligent Task Routing', and 'Post-Run Reflection'
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: All four sections start expanded when the page first loads. The section body content (e.g., 'Threshold (tokens)' label for Memory Compression, 'Max Retries' for Retry, 'Simple Tasks Model' for Routing, and the cyan info box for Post-Run Reflection) is visible without any user interaction.
assertions.precondition: Page has just loaded for the first time

groups.name: Loading State
groups.description: On mount, the page concurrently fetches agentic settings via get_agentic_settings (Tauri IPC) and reflection settings via GET /reflection/settings (HTTP). During the fetch, a loading indicator replaces the full form. This group verifies loading and transition-to-loaded behavior.

assertions.description: While settings are being fetched, an element with data-content-label 'loading agentic settings' is present and displays the text 'Loading agentic settings...'
assertions.precondition: Page has just mounted and the get_agentic_settings fetch has not yet completed

assertions.description: After both get_agentic_settings and /reflection/settings fetch complete, the loading indicator disappears and is replaced by the four collapsible section headers and the Save/Reset buttons
assertions.precondition: Page has just mounted

groups.name: Memory Compression Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a toggle switch in the header. When expanded (default), it shows four number inputs in a 2-column grid: Threshold (tokens), Target (tokens), Keep Recent Items, Summarize Batch Size. All inputs are disabled when the toggle is off. An info box explains the behavior. Defaults: enabled=true, threshold=80000, target=60000, keep_recent=5, batch_size=10.

assertions.description: The Memory Compression section header shows the subtitle 'Automatically compress context to prevent token overflow'

criteria.textContent: Automatically compress context to prevent token overflow

assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: When Memory Compression is expanded, a label 'Threshold (tokens)' is visible above a number input with min=10000, max=200000, step=5000. Its help text reads 'Compress when context exceeds this token count'.
assertions.precondition: Memory Compression section is expanded

assertions.description: When expanded, a label 'Target (tokens)' is visible with help text 'Target token count after compression'. The input has min=5000, max=150000, step=5000.
assertions.precondition: Memory Compression section is expanded

assertions.description: When expanded, a blue info box contains the text 'Memory compression prevents context overflow by summarizing old knowledge entries when the token count exceeds the threshold. Recent items are always preserved.'

criteria.textContent: Memory compression prevents context overflow by summarizing

assertions.precondition: Memory Compression section is expanded

assertions.description: When the Memory Compression toggle switch is turned off, all four number inputs (Threshold, Target, Keep Recent Items, Summarize Batch Size) become disabled and visually dimmed (opacity-50). Turning the toggle back on re-enables all four inputs. This prevents editing parameters that are ignored while compression is disabled.
assertions.precondition: Memory Compression section is expanded

assertions.description: Clicking the Memory Compression section header button toggles the body. When collapsed, the four inputs and info box are hidden. When expanded, they appear. The chevron icon faces down when expanded and right when collapsed.
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

groups.name: Retry with Feedback Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a toggle switch in the header. When expanded (default), it shows four number inputs (Max Retries, Base Delay, Max Delay, Exponential Base) in a 2-column grid, then two toggle rows (Add Jitter, Feedback Injection), then a yellow info box. All inputs and inner toggles are disabled when the master toggle is off. Defaults: enabled=true, max_retries=3, base_delay=1000ms, max_delay=30000ms, exp_base=2.0, jitter=true, feedback_injection=true.

assertions.description: The Retry with Feedback section header shows the subtitle 'Automatically retry on transient errors with context injection'

criteria.textContent: Automatically retry on transient errors with context injection

assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: When expanded, a label 'Max Retries' is visible with help text 'Maximum retry attempts'. The input has min=1, max=10.
assertions.precondition: Retry with Feedback section is expanded

assertions.description: When expanded, a label 'Exponential Base' is visible with help text 'Delay multiplier: base_delay * base^attempt'. The input has min=1.1, max=4, step=0.1.
assertions.precondition: Retry with Feedback section is expanded

assertions.description: When expanded, two toggle rows appear below the numeric inputs: 'Add Jitter' (with description 'Add random variation to prevent thundering herd') and 'Feedback Injection' (with description 'Include error context in retry prompts for learning'). Both toggles default to enabled.
assertions.precondition: Retry with Feedback section is expanded

assertions.description: When expanded, a yellow info box contains the text 'Retry handles transient errors like timeouts, rate limits, and connection issues. Feedback injection helps the AI learn from previous failures.'

criteria.textContent: Retry handles transient errors like timeouts, rate limits

assertions.precondition: Retry with Feedback section is expanded

assertions.description: When the Retry with Feedback master toggle is turned off, all four number inputs and both inner toggle rows (Add Jitter, Feedback Injection) become disabled. The inner toggles are rendered with opacity-50 and cannot be clicked. This matches the disabled={!settings.retry.enabled} prop applied to all child inputs and toggles.
assertions.precondition: Retry with Feedback section is expanded

groups.name: Intelligent Task Routing Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a toggle switch in the header. When expanded (default), it shows three model select dropdowns (Simple Tasks Model, Medium Tasks Model, Complex Tasks Model) and two file-count threshold number inputs (Simple Threshold, Medium Threshold). All controls are disabled when the master toggle is off. The model dropdowns each contain six Claude model options. Defaults: enabled=false, simple=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, medium=claude-sonnet-4-20250514, complex=claude-opus-4-20250514, file_count_thresholds=[3, 10].

assertions.description: The Intelligent Task Routing section header shows the subtitle 'Route tasks to different models based on complexity'

criteria.textContent: Route tasks to different models based on complexity

assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: When expanded, three labeled dropdowns appear: 'Simple Tasks Model' (with green sparkle icon and help text 'Quick fixes, small changes, formatting (fast/cheap)'), 'Medium Tasks Model' (yellow sparkle, 'Feature additions, bug fixes, moderate refactoring (balanced)'), and 'Complex Tasks Model' (purple sparkle, 'Architecture changes, major refactoring, security audits (powerful)').
assertions.precondition: Intelligent Task Routing section is expanded

assertions.description: Each model dropdown contains exactly six options: 'Claude 4.5 Haiku (Fast/Cheap)' (claude-haiku-4-5-20251001), 'Claude 3.5 Haiku (Legacy)' (claude-3-5-haiku-20241022), 'Claude Sonnet 4 (Balanced)' (claude-sonnet-4-20250514), 'Claude Opus 4 (Powerful)' (claude-opus-4-20250514), 'Claude 3.5 Sonnet (Legacy)' (claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022), and 'Claude 3 Opus (Legacy)' (claude-3-opus-20240229).

assertions.description: When expanded, a purple info box contains the text 'Task routing optimizes cost and latency by using faster/cheaper models for simple tasks. Complexity is assessed based on file count, prompt length, and keywords.'

criteria.textContent: Task routing optimizes cost and latency

assertions.precondition: Intelligent Task Routing section is expanded

assertions.description: The Intelligent Task Routing toggle defaults to OFF (enabled=false in DEFAULT_ROUTING_SETTINGS). When off, all three model dropdowns and both threshold inputs are visually dimmed and non-interactive. This is the only one of the four sections that defaults to disabled.
assertions.precondition: Settings have just loaded with default values

groups.name: Post-Run Reflection Section
groups.description: A collapsible panel with a toggle switch in the header. Unlike the other three sections, toggling Reflection saves immediately via PUT /reflection/settings to the runner's HTTP API — there is no separate Save button needed. When expanded (default), it shows only a cyan info box explaining the automated analysis behavior. Reflection settings are loaded from GET /reflection/settings (HTTP), not from Tauri IPC.

assertions.description: The Post-Run Reflection section header shows the subtitle 'Automatically analyze completed workflows to identify systemic issues and apply fixes'

criteria.textContent: Automatically analyze completed workflows to identify systemic issues

assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: When expanded, a cyan info box contains the text 'When enabled, the system automatically reviews completed workflow runs to detect recurring failures, inefficient patterns, and systemic issues.'

criteria.textContent: When enabled, the system automatically reviews completed workflow runs

assertions.precondition: Post-Run Reflection section is expanded

assertions.description: The cyan info box also contains the text 'Reflection can apply fixes such as knowledge base updates, workflow step rewrites, selector corrections, and instruction clarifications — improving future runs without manual intervention.'

criteria.textContent: Reflection can apply fixes such as knowledge base updates

assertions.precondition: Post-Run Reflection section is expanded

assertions.description: Toggling the Post-Run Reflection switch immediately calls PUT /reflection/settings with body { reflection_enabled: <new_value> }. On success the toggle stays in its new state and the onLog function logs 'Post-run reflection enabled' or 'Post-run reflection disabled'. On HTTP failure the toggle reverts to its previous state — no manual Save button press is needed for Reflection.
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded and the runner's HTTP API is reachable

assertions.description: Post-Run Reflection is stored and loaded via the runner's HTTP API (/reflection/settings), not via the same Tauri IPC commands used for the other three subsystems. Its state is NOT included in save_agentic_settings or get_agentic_settings. Consequently, clicking 'Save Agentic Settings' does not affect the Reflection toggle, and 'Reset to Defaults' does not reset the Reflection toggle.

groups.name: Action Buttons — Save and Reset
groups.description: Two action buttons appear at the bottom of the page in a flex row. 'Reset to Defaults' (left, muted background) restores Memory Compression, Retry, and Routing settings in-memory to their default values without saving. 'Save Agentic Settings' (right, primary background) calls save_agentic_settings and shows three sequential button states: idle with Brain icon, in-flight with spinner + 'Saving...', and success with check icon + 'Saved!'. A green success banner appears above the sections on success. Reset does NOT affect Post-Run Reflection.

assertions.description: A 'Save Agentic Settings' button with a Brain icon is present at the bottom right of the page
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: A 'Reset to Defaults' button is present at the bottom left of the page
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: Clicking 'Save Agentic Settings' transitions through three states: (1) default — Brain icon + 'Save Agentic Settings', (2) in-flight — spinner + 'Saving...' (button disabled), (3) success — check icon + 'Saved!'. After success, a green banner 'Settings saved successfully!' appears above the sections and auto-dismisses after 3 seconds. The button then returns to the default idle state.
assertions.precondition: Settings have loaded

assertions.description: Clicking 'Reset to Defaults' immediately restores all form fields in-memory to: compression.enabled=true, threshold_tokens=80000, target_tokens=60000, keep_recent_items=5, summarize_batch_size=10; retry.enabled=true, max_retries=3, base_delay_ms=1000, max_delay_ms=30000, exponential_base=2.0, jitter=true, feedback_injection=true; routing.enabled=false, simple_model=claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, medium_model=claude-sonnet-4-20250514, complex_model=claude-opus-4-20250514, file_count_thresholds=[3,10]. The page updates visually without a backend call. A subsequent Save is required to persist these defaults. Post-Run Reflection toggle is NOT reset.
assertions.precondition: Settings have been modified from their defaults

groups.name: Feedback Alerts — Error and Success
groups.description: The page shows contextual alerts in the form area (above the section panels, below the header) in response to save operations. Success alerts auto-dismiss after 3 seconds. Error alerts persist until the next save attempt clears them.

assertions.description: After a successful save operation (save_agentic_settings returns success=true), a green alert appears containing a check icon and the text 'Settings saved successfully!'. It automatically disappears after approximately 3 seconds.
assertions.precondition: A save operation has just completed successfully

assertions.description: If the save_agentic_settings Tauri command returns success=false or throws, a red error alert appears at the top of the form area displaying the backend's error message string. The alert persists until the next save attempt clears it by setting error=null at the start of a new save.

target.label: Settings page heading (error alert appears below it)

assertions.precondition: A save operation has returned an error from the Tauri backend

groups.name: Settings Persistence and Data Model
groups.description: Agentic settings (compression, retry, routing) are persisted via save_agentic_settings Tauri IPC and loaded via get_agentic_settings. The reflection toggle is persisted independently via PUT /reflection/settings HTTP. This group verifies round-trip integrity and the semantic contract of the settings objects.

assertions.description: After saving modified settings (e.g., compression.enabled=false, retry.max_retries=5, routing.enabled=true with medium_model changed to 'Claude Opus 4 (Powerful)'), navigating to a different Settings tab and returning to 'Advanced AI' should show all saved values still applied in the form — no reversion to defaults.
assertions.precondition: Settings have been saved and the user navigated away and back

assertions.description: The save_agentic_settings Tauri command receives camelCase parameters: compressionEnabled, compressionThresholdTokens (10000–200000), compressionTargetTokens (5000–150000), compressionKeepRecentItems (1–20), compressionSummarizeBatchSize (5–50), retryEnabled, retryMaxRetries (1–10), retryBaseDelayMs (100–10000), retryMaxDelayMs (1000–120000), retryExponentialBase (1.1–4.0), retryJitter, retryFeedbackInjection, routingEnabled, routingSimpleModel, routingMediumModel, routingComplexModel, routingFileThresholdSimple (1–20), routingFileThresholdMedium (2–50). The reflection toggle is excluded from this command. The UI enforces bounds with Math.max/Math.min clamping before calling save.

When get_agentic_settings returns a partial settings object (e.g., missing some fields added in a newer version), the component merges the response with DEFAULT_COMPRESSION_SETTINGS, DEFAULT_RETRY_SETTINGS, and DEFAULT_ROUTING_SETTINGS using spread operators. This ensures new fields are never undefined in the UI even if the backend hasn't been updated.
